glm.feedback:
Findings:

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: server/src/external/org/proposed-line.ts:79 (the added `evidenceQuote` needle line) and proposed-grammar.ts `parseEvidence`
  Finding: The spec/contract says the Evidence-line quote is 24–200 characters, but neither `parseEvidence` nor the guard enforces any minimum length. A short quote (e.g. `s1:...:3 — "ok"`) becomes a `foldForCompare` needle, and any edited proposed line that merely contains that common substring is then refused with 400 `line_contains_quote` — a false refusal that blocks countersign entirely (the entry stays, no way to accept it with any reasonable line). The fence-quote needles had the `> text — pointer` shape as an implicit length/structure constraint; the Evidence-line needle has none.
  Suggestion: In `proposalFacts`, only add the Evidence-quote needle when the quote meets the contract's minimum (e.g. ≥24 chars), or skip needles below some fold-length threshold so short quotes cannot block countersign.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/orgProposedGrammar.ts:204 / server/.../proposed-grammar.ts:203 (`EVIDENCE_QUOTE_RE`)
  Finding: A known pointer followed by ` — ""` (empty quote) yields quote `null` but the trimmed `source` is parsed from `m[1]` while the fallback path calls `parseSourceRef(raw)` on the *untrimmed* original — behaviorally equivalent here, but the two paths can diverge if `parseSourceRef` ever treats whitespace differently (e.g. a padded pointer like ` s1:…:3 — "q"`: the quote path trims, the old path didn't). This is a mild inconsistency, not a concrete failure given current `parseSourceRef`.
  Suggestion: Use `parseSourceRef(t)` in the fallback so both paths see the same trimmed input.

Test quality: the tests are substantive — they exercise real parse, guard-refusal (including case-folded repetition), audit content, and pin the fixture by hash and structure. The client unit tests would catch a wrong-quotes-order or markup regression. The e2e only covers display; guard/audit are covered server-side, which matches the AC's division. Note the second countersign test asserts the edited-line pass but does not assert the audit `data.evidence` lacks a `quote` field name — acceptable, since `not.toContain(QUOTE)` covers the text.

Regression risk: `proposalFacts`'s `pointer` variable was renamed to `source` destructuring; if `pointer` is referenced further down in the file (not shown), the diff context implies it compiles, and the exported API shapes are unchanged. `parseEvidence` is additive. No visible breakage for callers.

Spec compliance: all three AC behaviors (display-first plain text with source, copy-refusal guard, audit names source without quote) are implemented and tested. The hash pin and contract doc update match the referenced fixture.

Overall assessment: the work is sound and well-tested; the unenforced minimum quote length turning into a guard needle is the only defect worth fixing before or shortly after ship.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
